My investment research workflow started in a cloud-managed project. It brought together company filings, previous summaries, project instructions, and global skills for recurring tasks. A single Markdown document covered business research themes, accounting definitions, financial ratios, source preferences, and report structure.

That arrangement made it easy to get started. As the project grew, however, definitions, calculations, interpretations, and formatting instructions became intertwined. Some important decisions remained implicit.

Three opportunities motivated the move to a GitHub repository: testing changes, tracing errors, and breaking research into manageable steps.

Testing different versions
